result.summary: REAL, ON-DISK EVIDENCE FOR THIS STEP: test/reports/report-2026-09-03-REQ214.yaml's own 'first_attempt' section (preserved verbatim in that file, confirmed present on disk at reconstruction time). This handoff file itself is a RECONSTRUCTION written 2026-09-03 after the fact, reformatting that real report's own first_attempt content into this schema -- not a fresh invention. Timestamps are reconstructed approximations except where noted below, where they are copied directly from the real report. Full-suite run: combined 3090 tests, 6 properties, 5 failures (3091/3096 passed) -- verbatim from the real report. 5 failures, in 2 classes. CLASS 1 (1 failure, REAL DEFECT, THIS BRANCH): Letflow.Engine.ServiceTaskDispatcherTest's boot-gating describe block -- specifically the 'config/dev.exs does not override start_service_task_dispatcher to false' test -- crashed under scripts/test_parallel.sh's MIX_TEST_PARTITION env var. Root cause: the test used Config.Reader.read!/1 against config/dev.exs directly, which executes that file's own content -- and config/dev.exs carries a deliberate ISS-0015 (GH#71) guard that raises whenever MIX_TEST_PARTITION is set, specifically to stop dev config from silently loading under partitioned test runs. This test's own approach (Config.Reader.read!/1, safe for config/prod.exs which carries no such guard) was the wrong technique for config/dev.exs specifically, and the failure is a real, reproducible defect in this branch's own new test file, not a flake. CLASS 2 (4 failures, attributed to environmental contention, NOT this branch): 3x Letflow.TenantSchemaReaperTest (concurrent-invocation liveness guard / reclaims orphaned row / schema_name format guard) and 1x Letflow.Engine.Lua.ExecutorTest (configurable memory limit, nil max_heap_words) -- attributed to Postgres too_many_connections pressure from concurrent sibling sessions on this host, structurally unrelated to this branch's diff (git diff confirms neither test/support/tenant_schema_reaper_test.exs nor test/letflow/engine/lua/executor_test.exs is touched by this branch's changes). This attribution is stated as an attribution, not a certainty -- the real report's own note says these tests were never claimed to fail deterministically, only under measured contention, and this is independently re-checked in the rerun (see step-04-recheck1.json).
